name: Angela Davis
role: American philosopher, activist and author; prison abolitionist and socialist (born 1944)
summary: Angela Davis is a Marxist-influenced scholar and activist who joined the Communist Party USA in 1968 and has long argued that racism is bound up with capitalism. She is a leading advocate of abolishing prisons and policing, supports Palestinian rights and BDS, and describes feminism and anti-racism as inseparable from class struggle. She has favored socialist revolution while taking part in electoral politics, and in 2020 backed Joe Biden as the candidate more open to pressure from movements.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her abolitionist alternatives in the 2003 book include a health system providing free physical and mental care to all; in 2021 she lamented the privatization of hospitals and health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Lists job and living-wage programs among alternatives to imprisonment; she never addressed the size of a minimum-wage rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues that racism cannot be ended with capitalism left in place and calls for movement toward socialist organization of the economy; treats capitalism as built on exploitation.

unions-good.rationale: Describes unions and socialist and communist organizing as part of the 'other America' that expanded democracy, and wants a party grounded in labor.

cut-welfare.rationale: Criticizes the disestablishment of welfare and of the economic safety net, and lists alternatives to the dismantled welfare program among abolitionist measures.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Backs decriminalizing drug use, from marijuana to heroin, paired with free voluntary treatment; she speaks of decriminalization as a step toward abolition, not of a legal retail market.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In a 1975 interview she excludes racist advocacy denying others' right to exist from protected democratic speech; the view is old and not stated as a call for legal restriction.

state-harmful.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

empower-police-military.rationale: Calls police and prisons institutions to be cast into the dustbin of history, supports defunding the police, and says violence-based safety is not safety; also challenges militarism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Names sex work with drug use as behavior to decriminalize by repealing laws penalizing those who work in the sex industry, as a step toward decarceration.

rehabilitation.rationale: Proposes justice based on reparation and reconciliation rather than retribution and vengeance, within a broader abolitionist aim; she rejects prisons altogether rather than endorsing reformed ones.

traditional-family.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She supports marriage equality as a civil-rights demand while seeking a more radical transformation.

abortion-legal.rationale: Wrote that individual choice, contraception and abortions when necessary are a fundamental prerequisite for women's emancipation, and called the 1973 legalization a victory while criticizing sterilization abuse.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Throughout her career argues society must restructure to incorporate formerly enslaved people, citing Du Bois on Reconstruction, and calls for confronting the history of racism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Says the narrow gender binary reflects how gender has been ideologically produced and reproduced, and wants a world in which binary gender no longer governs segregation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposes the border wall, immigrant detention and the criminalization of undocumented immigrants, and says immigrants who live here ought to vote.

nation-first.rationale: Describes her politics as internationalist and warns against only thinking about people in this country; calls for a revived socialist internationalism.

open-borders.rationale: Asks listeners to imagine a world without xenophobia and the fenced-in borders, and says the nation-state is becoming obsolete; she does not outline a specific open-borders policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: In 1972 said liberation means overturning capitalism through a socialist revolution; in 2020 said abolition is about revolution.

military-superiority.rationale: Lists militarism and war among the structures a transformative feminism must challenge.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

direct-action.rationale: Says she prefers building mass movements that pressure whoever holds office, yet also says people must take part in elections, so evidence is mixed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Says democratic relationships should be enacted in the course of struggling for change, including giving imprisoned people leadership, so activists become worthy of the world they seek.

production-for-use.rationale: Her closing vision makes access to food independent of capitalist profit requirements.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Says a more socialist economy is needed to replace a system based on exploitation and super-exploitation of racialized workers, drawing on Marx on primitive accumulation.

positive-liberty.rationale: She distinguishes substantive freedom through jobs, education, healthcare and housing from formal civil rights alone.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Supports BDS, calls Israel's policies apartheid and Gaza a genocide, and welcomes people standing up to Zionism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: She calls for economic democracy with everyone participating in governing the economy; she does not speak to votes in large companies specifically.

class-collaboration.rationale: Her account makes exploitation inherent in the capitalist employment relationship, rather than a partnership of shared interests.

workers-nation.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Grew up in segregated Birmingham, opposed segregation throughout her career, and described imagining a world without racial segregation as part of her own history.

state-class-instrument.rationale: She describes the modern state as a product of bourgeois revolutions and capitalism sustained through repressive institutions; she does not say it is only a ruling-class tool.

national-mission.rationale: She criticizes the US democratic-model narrative used to justify interventions and drone killings abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Names hetero-patriarchy among the systems of domination alongside white supremacy and capitalism, and her books argue women's subordination is structural.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Calls Palestine a microcosm of colonialism, racial capitalism and apartheid.

consent-of-governed.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

death-penalty.rationale: Links the campaign to abolish the death penalty to prison abolition and says the death penalty should be abolished.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Treated the Soviet Union as a socialist country that had solved national oppression (1972) and later said its states made amazing gains for people's lives despite lacking political democracy.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Describes affirmative action as a legitimate collective strategy meant to change structures of discrimination, and criticizes neoliberal arguments against it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Told an interviewer she completely agreed that nonhuman animals must be included in democratic concern, linking the brutalization of animals to that of people.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Her Civil War analysis centers emancipation and enslaved workers’ withdrawal of labor as decisive to the conflict.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: She treats taking down racist statues as part of rethinking and replacing oppressive institutions.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: She describes contemporary institutional racism as operating without explicitly racist laws or attitudes through unequal access and incarceration.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: She expresses support for radical LGBTQ movements seeking abolition of marriage as a capitalist institution; this is support for those movements, not a stated call of her own.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: She locates women’s oppression in reproductive labor and global capitalist production, requiring structural transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: She endorses free daycare centers and says women across the country need them more than ever.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: She explicitly retains a communist identification and socialist alternative to capitalism after leaving the party.

suppress-opposition.rationale: She advocates protecting independent movements from state repression; her later departure over party democratization reinforces that position.

participatory-democracy.rationale: She advocates everyone participating in government and economic life on equal terms.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: She insists race, gender and class be analyzed and challenged together, rejecting a class-only approach.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: She emphasizes the centrality of defending trans people and their rights in prison.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: She states support for radical LGBTQ sectors calling for dismantling the military; this is support for others' call, not her own stated demand.

property-franchise.rationale: She criticizes the original franchise restricted to affluent white men as minority domination masquerading as democracy.

racial-franchise.rationale: She criticizes democracy limited to white men and calls for collective control by all inhabitants.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: She explicitly calls for replacing policing and imprisonment with ways to address the problems they fail to solve.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: She expressly says resident immigrants should vote because they belong to the community.

local-essentials-public.rationale: She criticizes privatized healthcare and argues hospitals must serve the public good; water and transport are not addressed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: She rejects defining democracy merely as political rule, insisting on social and economic equality.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: She explains commodity exchange value through socially necessary average labor time.

material-over-identity.rationale: She rejects reducing liberation to class alone and insists racial and gender struggles be central.

notes:
She said she had never voted for a major-party presidential candidate before Barack Obama. In 2016 she declined to endorse, and in 2020 she said she would not endorse but would vote Democratic to elect a candidate more amenable to movement pressure. The 1972 Soviet answers are from her youth; by 2008 she acknowledged those states lacked political democracy.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 36 answers taken from it, 16 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; old audit consulted only for notes/source list. Full 2003 book and long interviews downloaded and searched by theme. All 490 statements and every remaining null reviewed. No inference from Communist Party membership. Her earlier praise of Soviet authorities and refusal to support dissidents are relevant controversies, documented in the scholarly source; her later account of leaving the CP over internal democratization and her 2020–2024 democratic commitments are used for current views. Opposition to party restrictions internally does not itself establish a position on multiparty government. Support for online organizing does not answer online governmental deliberation. Anti-Monsanto rhetoric does not establish a view on genetic engineering. General internationalism does not answer specific supranational or world-economic designs. No legacy-list decision made. Final specificity review removed private-prison criticism as insufficient for the broader private courts/defense proposition, forced-sterilization criticism as insufficient for heritable-defect policy, and particular US intervention criticism as insufficient to settle all humanitarian intervention. Modern socialist commitment is not evidence about capitalism’s capacity to avoid collapse. The priority list yields only consent-of-governed and suppress-opposition.
